item.title: Reacts poll: Throw it to Bryant more
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Wide receiver Pat Bryant (13) of the Denver Broncos pulls in a catch while cornerback Taron Johnson (3) of the Las Vegas Raiders bears down on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images While Steelers fans are still figuring out WTF just happened with their team in the last five days, Broncos fans are wondering when Pat Bryant is going to become the primary target for Bo Nix. Well, that may be an exaggeration, but Broncos Country does believe No. 13 is the most reliable receiver on a team with a slew of pass-catchers. And the choice wasn’t even close. By a huge margin, Broncos fans think Bryant is one of the best targets for Nix. And by the numbers, they’re not wrong. With just 21 targets, Bryant has caught 16 this season for a total of 221 yards and 2TDs, for a 13.8 average on yards per catch. By comparison, Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton each have more total catches and yards, but the number of drops is much higher. Waddle is 33 of 58 for 398 yards and 2 TDs (12.8 ypc average) and Sutton is 25 of 48 for 266 yards and 2 TDs (10.6 ypc). No wonder only 15% of fans picked Sutton as most reliable and just 1% said Waddle, the receiver who is supposed to be our new super star. Not surprisingly, when Nix is throwing to Bryant his passer rating is gooooooooood . This is wild: Bo Nix has a 146 passer rating when targeting Pat Bryant this year. pic.twitter.com/MoEfU7ATsA — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 26, 2026 While the Broncos have a lot of receiving targets — and all want the ball — second-year Bryant has earned a few more targets than the rest.

item.title: Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Sends Brian Schottenheimer Message After Eagles Loss
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys suffered a 39-38 defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving . It was their second loss in the last three games despite leading by 21 points. Team owner Jerry Jones send a message about Brian Schottenheimer during his postgame interview. He was promoted to head coach on Jan. 24, 2025, after previously serving as the team’s offensive coordinator. Schottenheimer guided the franchise to a 7-9-1 record in his first year in charge and missed the playoffs for the second straight season. Dallas dropped to 5-7 this campaign and remain in third place in the NFC East. The Eagles are trailing them by half-a-game, while the New York Giants continue to led the division with a 6-3 record. Oct 8, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones speaks to the media before the game at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Jerry Jones opens up on potentially replacing Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer Jerry Jones made it clear that his team doesn’t plan on making a coaching change soon. He added that the focus should be on the upcoming games. “The game where it was ours to take and we didn’t,” Jones said. “So when you look at every whatever, then you have to question everything… You’ve got to look at everything. And that’s certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time. We’ve got several more games to go and we’ve got to have our mind on that.” Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 The 84-year-old added that Dallas has a bigger chance of winning with Brian Schottenheimer in charge. “No, I wouldn’t anticipate that,” Jones said . At this juncture, we can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games, and be where competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time.” The Cowboys have 11 days before they play their next game on Dec. 7. They will visit the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, at Lumen Field in a high-stakes matchup. ABC will broadcast the “Monday Night Football” game live at 8:15 p.m. ET. item.title: Freiburg in ecstasy as remarkable winning streak extends to six matches
item.description: Freiburg in ecstasy as remarkable winning streak extends to six matches SC Freiburg head coach Julian Schuster has praised his squad’s extraordinary team spirit following Thursday evening’s dramatic 2-1 Conference League victory over FC Twente. The Breisgauer secured their sixth consecutive competitive victory thanks to a stoppage-time winner from Niklas Beste, with Schuster emphasizing the importance of a united dressing room in navigating a demanding schedule. The Freiburg trainer made six changes to the starting XI that defeated Elversberg 1-0 in the Bundesliga last weekend. Cyriaque Irié rewarded Schuster’s faith by scoring the opener in the 11th minute, but Twente remained the more threatening side for much of the first half and eventually equalized through a Younes Taha free kick in the 62nd. Freiburg nevertheless found another way to win. Substitute Derry Scherhant earned a penalty in the 89th minute, and fellow replacement Beste eventually converted the loose ball after Matthias Ginter’s spot kick struck the post. Schuster explains how Freiburg’s team spirit enables squad rotation Speaking to a group of assembled journalists after the post-match press conference, Schuster drew attention to the collective celebrations following Beste’s dramatic winner. The 41-year-old suggested that the team’s togetherness gives him the confidence to rotate extensively without compromising Freiburg’s competitiveness. “That scene in which the team celebrated together is emblematic of this group,” Schuster told the journalists. “That lends us the strength to rotate the squad with full confidence. One sees this with various clubs that have to deal with extreme pressure during this phase [of the season]. There’s also players who have international obligations. The pressure is extreme. “One really can’t leave anyone out,” Schuster continued. “We have this depth and there’s always little things that leave one needing to switch it up. Then it’s nice when players are ready to serve on a regular basis and not to get caught up in the competition of who makes the team sheet. That’s extremely important and I’m very pleased with the lads who started today and were able to make a contribution to the win.” Schuster’s observations build on his earlier comments concerning Freiburg’s exceptional dressing-room culture . In October, the SC trainer emphasized the importance of protecting the club’s special atmosphere and ensuring that difficult personnel decisions do not undermine the collective. The same philosophy has also been emphasized by Freiburg’s players. Veteran midfielder Maximilian Eggestein recently discussed the importance of sacrificing individual ambitions for the team , while Germany internationals Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant credited Freiburg’s supportive club culture when reflecting on their own development. item.title: Josh Uche’s Homecoming: How the Miami Native Found His Footing Again with the Dolphins
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images For Miami Dolphins edge rusher Josh Uche , the 2026 NFL season has been more than just another stop on a winding professional journey—it has been a long-awaited homecoming. Signed to a one-year contract in March after bouncing across three teams in two years, the 28-year-old Miami native has quietly re-emerged as a reliable, every-down contributor for a rebuilding Dolphins defense. Early Promise and Breakout in New England Drafted by the New England Patriots in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of the University of Michigan, Uche quickly earned a reputation as an explosive, twitchy pass-rush specialist. After battling injuries and adjusting to the pro game over his first two seasons, he exploded onto the scene in 2022. Operating alongside Matthew Judon, Uche racked up 11.5 sacks and two forced fumbles in 15 games, looking every bit like a cornerstone defender for New England’s future. Two Years of Uncertainty However, replicating that 2022 magic proved difficult. Following a three-sack 2023 campaign, Uche re-signed with New England on a short-term deal before being shipped to the Kansas City Chiefs at the 2024 trade deadline. In Kansas City, Uche struggled to crack Steve Spagnuolo’s defensive rotation, appearing in just six games without recording a sack. Seeking a fresh start in 2025, he signed with the Philadelphia Eagles . While he generated solid pressure rates in limited passing-down snaps, he finished the year with just one sack across 12 appearances, leaving his NFL trajectory at a crossroads entering free agency. Reviving His Career in South Florida When Miami brought Uche home in March 2026, the move flew largely under the radar. Initially viewed as a low-cost depth addition to a revamped linebacker room, Uche has outperformed expectations. Through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season, Uche has already surpassed his combined sack total from the previous two campaigns: Defensive Production: 38 total tackles, 3.0 sacks, 24 total quarterback pressures, and one forced fumble. Expanded Role: Rather than being pigeonholed strictly as a third-down specialist, Uche has logged over 420 defensive snaps and earned strong marks for his run defense—proving he can hold the edge on early downs as well as collapse the pocket. Looking Ahead For a Dolphins squad navigating roster turnover and key injuries during the 2026 campaign, Uche’s steady play has been a bright spot. Returning to the AFC East—and getting the chance to square off against his former Patriots squad twice a year—has given the South Florida product a renewed edge. As Miami enters the final stretch of the season, Uche is making a compelling case that his best football is still ahead of him right in his own backyard. item.title: Eagles player wasn’t wanted in Dallas. Now he’s getting the last laugh: ‘Packing their bags’
item.description: ARLINGTON, Texas — Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott joked before Thursday’s game that Eagles quarterback Joe Milton was “still a Cowboy” and would help Dallas win. Prescott’s wishes did not come true. Milton crushed the Cowboys and outplayed Prescott, a four-time Pro Bowl quarterback. The Cowboys cut Milton on Aug. 31, and two months later, he left Dallas’ practice squad to join the Eagles’ 53-man roster after Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots. In his third start with Philadelphia, Milton led the Eagles to a 39-38 comeback victory over the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed for a touchdown. “Resilience,” Eagles wide receiver Elijah Moore said of Milton’s performance. “I’m sure that they probably didn’t think the outcome of the game, especially at the end of the game, was going to end up like that. I’m pretty sure that they were probably packing their bags, going inside. And obviously early in the game when it was 31 to 10, they probably thought it was over with. So Joe showed that you never give up. And [if] you continue to sleep [on them], players that you once had are going to come outshine them for another team. And that’s exactly what he showed.” The Eagles looked finished after the Cowboys took a 31-10 lead with 3:40 remaining in the third quarter. But then came Milton. He threw a 45-yard touchdown to DeVonta Smith with 24 seconds left in the third quarter, making it 31-17. He cut Dallas’ lead to eight points (38-30) after rushing for a 15-yard touchdown with 9:17 left in the fourth quarter. On the next drive, he connected with rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a two-point game (38-36) with 2:17 left on the clock. On the Eagles’ last offensive possession, Milton completed two passes to set up Philadelphia’s game-winning field goal. Milton said there was a “lot going through his head” knowing that he was playing against his former team, but he looked unfazed by the moment. Late in the second quarter, the Eagles trailed 21-3 when Milton rolled to his left and threw a 50-yard touchdown to Smith. On that throw, Milton dropped back to the 40-yard line and launched the ball 64.4 yards in the air, the longest touchdown by an Eagles quarterback in the Next Gen Stats era (2016), according to ESPN insights. According to Next Gen Stats, Milton completed 4 of 6 deep passes (20 or more yards) from outside the pocket for 139 yards and three touchdowns, which is the most yards and touchdowns on deep throws in the NGS era. “Heck, yeah, like everybody,” Eagles running back Will Shipley said when asked if he was amazed by Milton’s throws. “Half the time in protection, I’ll look back, the ball will be in the air, and I’m just like, ‘Holy cow.’ I feel like I’m watching it like it’s on TV, but there’s just so much belief in 14 [Joe Milton’s number]. … Everyone in this locker room believes in him as the leader of this team. item.title: Morrison confident Price will 'heal quickly'
item.description: Isaac Price is West Bromwich Albion's top goalscorer in the Championship with seven goals [Getty Images] West Bromwich Albion manager James Morrison is hopeful Isaac Price can return to action ahead of schedule after the midfielder was ruled out for up to six weeks with a knee injury. The 23-year-old came off with an issue in the second half of last Saturday's 2-2 draw at Championship rivals Swansea City . Baggies head coach James Morrison has now confirmed that Price has suffered a grade two medial ligament injury. "He'll be out for roughly six weeks maximum. But, knowing Pricey, he heals quickly," Morrison told BBC Radio WM. "He's a great athlete and a great professional. I'm hoping he'll be a little bit quicker." Coming on top of Mali's Ousmane Diakite being injured on international duty , it leaves Albion light in midfield for Saturday's visit of Bristol City (15:00 GMT) as Rabby Nzingoula misses the game through suspension after being booked in the 3-1 midweek win at Bolton , his fifth yellow card in nine games. "It's something I'll have to speak to him about as three of them could have been avoided," Morrison added. If Price is out for the entire six weeks, he could potentially miss two key encounters with promotion rivals Stoke City, against a meeting with fellow countrymen Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny, as well as fixtures against Portsmouth, Cardiff City, Sheffield United, Lincoln City and Preston North End. One option for Saturday is to redeploy left-back Callum Styles, who plays in central midfield for Hungary, but Morrison has also got other options, both short and long term. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The New York Knicks host the Miami Heat at Madison Square Garden on Friday, November 27, with the defending champions seeking their seventh consecutive victory. Tipoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. The Knicks are 12–6 and third in the Eastern Conference, while the Heat sit sixth at 10–7. New York beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 121–102 on Wednesday, while Miami’s seven-game winning streak ended with a 111–104 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers . There are NBA Cup implications, too. Miami can clinch Group B with a win and a 76ers loss. The Knicks need a victory to avoid elimination. The Knicks have the stronger defensive foundation. Their 108.3 defensive rating ranks fifth, compared with Miami’s 24th-ranked 116.4. New York ranks eighth in net rating at +6.2 despite a 13th-ranked offensive rating of 114.4. That balance gives the Knicks more ways to survive stretches when shots stop falling. New York also ranks third in rebounding at 46.7 per game and fourth in three-point percentage at 37.4%. Its 14.9 made threes per game rank fourth. Those strengths offer a useful combination: punish defensive breakdowns from outside, then recover enough misses to keep possessions alive. Jalen Brunson leads the offense with 26.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 5.9 assists, shooting 42.7% overall and 39.6% from three. Miami cannot afford to let him repeatedly turn the corner and force its big men into difficult help decisions. New York can exploit that weakness by moving the ball after the initial drive, forcing Miami’s defenders to recover across the floor. Why The Heat Have The Advantage? Miami’s offense is a lot more productive. The Heat rank second in scoring at 119.7 points per game, second in assists at 29.3, and third in free-throw attempts at 28.8. Without Anunoby, New York would have fewer options for absorbing his drives before committing extra defenders. The Spartans head to Rutgers on Saturday afternoon as favorites in a game for the first time since week two. Michigan State is listed as a field goal favorite in this matchup, with the Spartans needing a win over the Scarlet Knights to avoid finishing in last place in the Big Ten. Both teams come into this matchup with 3-8 records and locked in to missing out on the bowl season this year. The Spartans lost last week against Oregon, while Rutgers stunned Penn State on the final play of the game to snap a four-game losing streak. item.title: Magnus Bradbury makes first Scotland start in a year against Argentina
item.description: Back-rower Magnus Bradbury will make his first start in a year for injury-hit Scotland in their Nations Championship finals weekend clash with Argentina at Allianz Stadium on Sunday. Head coach Gregor Townsend is unable to call on a string of senior players, including captain Sione Tuipulotu, Ben White, Pierre Schoeman, Scott Cummings, and back-row trio Matt Fagerson, Jack Dempsey and Jamie Ritchie . The absence of Fagerson and Dempsey has paved the way for Edinburgh forward Bradbury, who was not named in the initial squad for this month’s matches, to start in the number eight jersey for the first time since the victory over Tonga last November. The situation in the back-row has been improved by the fact flanker Rory Darge is fit enough to return and captain the side after a shoulder issue forced him to miss last weekend’s win over Japan . Rory Darge is fit enough to return and captain the side (Getty) After Townsend rotated his side heavily for that match, Blair Kinghorn , Kyle Steyn, Huw Jones and Finn Russell return to join Darcy Graham , Rory Hutchinson and Jamie Dobie in a more familiar-looking backline. In the front row, hooker Ewan Ashman returns and is joined by props Rory Sutherland and D’arcy Rae, with key man Zander Fagerson being kept in reserve for a big role off the bench. Gregor Brown and Jonny Gray retain their places together in the second row, while Josh Bayliss joins Darge and Bradbury in the back row, with last weekend’s hat-trick hero Liam McConnell dropping to the bench. George Horne and the versatile Tom Jordan are the two backs listed among the substitutes for a match that will effectively decide who finishes seventh in the inaugural Nations Championship. item.title: Ruben Amorim stunned as Omari Hutchinson sparks epic AC Milan Europa League turnaround
item.description: Udinese Calcio v AC Milan - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport AC Milan staged a stunning second-half fightback to beat Olympiacos 4-2 in Greece and revive their faltering Europa League campaign. Manager Ruben Amorim was quick to deflect tactical credit after watching one standout winger tear the hosts apart in a blistering 15-minute spell. Hutchinson inspires dramatic turnaround in Greece Hutchinson produced a goal and two assists to power Milan past Olympiacos in a thrilling Europa League clash . The Rossoneri overturned a two-goal deficit to claim a vital victory and keep their European hopes alive. Trailing 2-0 after Mike Maignan's own goal and a superb strike from Jota Silva, Milan looked destined for another damaging defeat. Hutchinson sparked the revival in the 56th minute, picking up possession near halfway, driving forward, cutting inside and firing calmly into the far corner. The winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser seven minutes later before creating the 71st-minute volley that saw substitute Christian Pulisic put Milan ahead. Diego Moreira sealed the 4-2 triumph in stoppage time on a counter-attack involving Pulisic. Amorim hands full credit to Hutchinson Following the final whistle, Amorim played down his own tactical adjustments and insisted Hutchinson's individual brilliance decided the contest. "I didn't change the game," the former Manchester United manager told reporters. "[Goncalo] Ramos came off because he was in pain, so it was a normal substitution. Hutchinson changed the game more than I did. What changed was the first goal." Amorim made it clear that such an influential display came as no surprise, while challenging the winger to maintain his high standards. "I always expect this from him," he added. "He has the potential to do much more. He has talent, like other players in the squad, but it's the head that counts." Milan avoid unwanted European history The victory arrived at a critical moment for the competition favourites, who had lost three of their opening four league-phase fixtures. Conceding twice in Greece also brought an unwelcome milestone, with Opta confirming Milan have now let in at least two goals in three consecutive European matches for the first time in club history. Despite those defensive concerns, Amorim believes the manner of the comeback can serve as a turning point for his squad. "It definitely changes our future," he said. "We did well in the second half, but we made a lot of mistakes again and we have to improve. We have a lot to do to become a very strong team, but the spirit is there. This is the start of something. To believe it, you have to see it. Today we saw that we came back from two goals down and won 4-2. Our confidence will grow." Rossoneri look to build momentum The three points lift Milan to 20th place in the Europa League standings, leaving them on six points from five league-phase matches. item.title: Eagles coach faces backlash for being ‘classless’ and ‘a loser,’ but his players love it
item.description: ARLINGTON, Texas — Eagles coach Nick Sirianni had every reason to be excited after his team overcame a 21-point deficit to beat the Cowboys on Thanksgiving, but many people are upset with how Sirianni conducted himself after the game. After Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made a game-winning field goal to complete the 39-38 win, Sirianni ran over to a group of Cowboys fans in the crowd and rubbed the victory in their faces. He had to be pulled away from the fans before shaking hands with Cowboys players and coaches at midfield. The social media reaction to Sirianni’s celebration has drawn criticism. One of Sirianni’s critics said, “Your team is 4-7, bro. What are you doing?” Sirianni’s answer to that question could be, “I just saved my job today.” Sirianni acted like a man who needed to let loose. Two weeks ago, he appeared to be on the hot seat after the Eagles lost seven consecutive games. But the Eagles have won their last two games and have looked better. If this keeps up, Sirianni’s job is likely safe this offseason. “Excited to celebrate,” Sirianni told reporters about his reaction after the game. “There were a lot of Eagles fans back there. I was excited to celebrate with those Eagles fans and our team. And everything like that. It was fun.” Sure. But what about those Cowboys fans who were sitting there? “I’m sure there were some in there,” Sirianni said. “But at that point, it felt like there were only Eagles fans. We were able to high-five. It was a fun experience there.” Sirianni’s players never stopped fighting after trailing 31-10 late in the third quarter. After quarterback Joe Milton and defensive tackle Ty Robinson made game-changing plays, the Eagles came back to win 39-38 over the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. It was one of Sirianni’s signature victories during his six seasons with Philadelphia, but he’s not receiving credit for it publicly. Instead, he’s getting ripped on social media platforms like X. Here are a few of the comments: “Nick Sirianni is classless and should not be an NFL head coach. Buddy needs a nap and an ice cream sandwich to go chill out.” “Nick Sirianni doesn’t deserve the wins this team gets. He’s such an embarrassment to NFL coaches. Imagine completing the biggest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history and then running to the SIDELINES to argue with fans!?” “My goodness, Sirianni is such a loser.” The outrage was loud, but Eagles players were not bothered by Sirianni’s actions. item.title: “She Should Be the Last Person Complaining About Referees”: NFL Fans React As Patrick Mahomes’ Wife Brittany Blasts Refs Over Controversial Officiating vs. Bills
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes greets wife, Brittany Mahomes, during warmups prior to the game against the Washington Commanders at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. © Reuters Connect The Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Buffalo Bills went down to the wire. Bills kicker Tyler Bass nailed a 57-yard field goal as the clock expired to seal a 13-10 win. However, shortly before the game-winning field goal, a controversial call against Rashee Rice stopped what could’ve been a promising Chiefs drive with the score tied at 10-10. On a 3rd-and-10 play, Rice leaped to catch a contested ball; however, as he fell to the ground, the ball touched the turf, and after review, the referees ruled it an incomplete pass. After the loss, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, took to social media to call out the officiating with a scathing message. “HAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE. Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us…Not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess?” she wrote on her Instagram story. Fans weren’t too pleased with her calling out the officials. One fan said : “She should be the last person complaining about referees lol.” Patrick Mahomes Makes Thoughts Clear on Nail-Biter Against Bills After suffering their third loss of the season, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes did not mince words about the team’s effort against a tough road opponent. During his post-game conference, Mahomes said : “I thought we battled through some adversity well, especially defensively. And we played a really good football team down to the wire. Obviously, we made too many mistakes, especially towards the end of the game, but throughout the game, that kind of cost us the victory. At the same time, I thought the guys did a great job of handling the weather, doing their best to kind of get things going, and we just came up short.” The Chiefs boasted a top-10 offense entering this game after dismantling the Arizona Cardinals in a 34-point performance on Sunday. However, the weather combined with a stout Bills defense shut down the team’s aerial attack, with Mahomes accounting for 174 yards. The Chiefs will now face the LA Rams on TNF next week, Dec. 3. item.title: Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua despite mental health concerns
item.description: FILE PHOTO - British boxer Tyson Fury celebrates his victory over Ukraine's Vladimir Klitschko after their world heavyweight title bout at the Esprit Arena in Duesseldorf. (is associated with: «Fury cleared to fight Anthony Joshua despite mental health concerns») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month despite concerns about his mental health. The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated earlier this week that it would investigate comments from Fury’s wife Paris that the boxer had been diagnosed with schizophrenia, and had the powers to deny him a licence to fight. However, Paris Fury retracted her claim in a statement issued on Thursday night, and the BBBoC’s general secretary Robert Smith told Sky Sports: “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning.” Paris Fury said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary due for release today that Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after beating Wladimir Klitschko to win the world heavyweight title in Dusseldorf in November 2015. She said in Thursday’s statement: “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Netflix indicated it had edited the footage as a result, saying in a statement: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a near three-year hiatus from boxing, with his weight ballooning to 27 stone, while he battled suicidal thoughts and alcohol addiction. Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

item.title: Michigan captain Rod Moore seeks one last win in Ohio State rivalry
item.description: ANN ARBOR – For players from Michigan and Ohio, The Game carries additional personal weight, but for Michigan safety and three-time captain Rod Moore, this upcoming game has multiple layers. Moore is from Dayton, Ohio, a little more than an hour’s drive from Ohio Stadium in Columbus, where Michigan and Ohio State will play on Saturday, Nov. 28, for the 122nd time in the series. His career with the Wolverines began in 2021 but was temporarily derailed and extended by a knee injury during spring practice in 2024 that sidelined him that season and for the better part of 2025. He joked with reporters this week that his college career could be a movie or a book. “Yeah, it’s been a lot,” Moore said. Moore is expected to play in The Game between Michigan and Ohio State one last time, although he was listed as “questionable” on the first Big Ten availability lists . “I'm going back home, maybe finishing my Michigan career back at home,” Moore said. “It's very important to me, especially because it's probably not the most even matchup — we both have our share of losses, our share of defeats this year. It's probably going to be the grittiest one I've been a part of, to be honest.” More: Trev Alberts' attorney plans to file lawsuit against Michigan There hasn’t been much national buzz for this matchup as Ohio State, which was ranked No. 1 in the preseason polls, is 7-4 overall, 5-3 Big Ten, and Michigan is 6-5, 3-5. Ohio State lost 31-28 at Nebraska, the Buckeyes ’ third loss in four games, sending them out of the College Football Playoff hunt. Michigan won the last two meetings at Ohio Stadium, including a 13-10 upset in 2024 when the No. 2 Buckeyes were three-touchdown favorites. item.description: Tyler Bass made NFL history with his right foot. James Cook ran into elite company. And the Buffalo Bills won a game in which Josh Allen threw two interceptions and didn't account for a touchdown. Buffalo overcame a sloppy offensive performance and miserable weather to beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving night, winning on Bass' 57-yard field goal as time expired. Bass became the first player in league history to make a game-tying field goal of at least 54 yards and a game-winning field goal of at least 54 yards in the fourth quarter of the same game. He connected from 54 yards with 11:58 remaining to tie the game 10-10. Then, with four seconds left and the game on the line, Bass drilled a 57-yarder as time expired to give Buffalo the victory. He did it in brutal conditions. The temperature was 34 degrees at kickoff, with wind gusts reaching 35 mph and rain falling throughout the night. James Cook joined Terry Allen in exclusive NFL club Cook has been running into the record books almost every week. He carried the ball 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City. It marked his 10th consecutive game with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown, tying Terry Allen for the longest streak in NFL history. Allen accomplished the feat with Washington across the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Bills are 10-1 for first time since 1991 It's been 35 years since the Bills started a season this well. item.title: Four Keys That Keep Miami Marlins Baseball Alive In 2026
item.description: Credit: Jeff Klein-Imagn Images Thanksgiving week arrives with a mix of gratitude and frustration for Miami fans. The Marlins did not reach the postseason, yet the roster holds enough talent to spark hope for the future. While the standings tell one story, the development of young players tells a much better one. The front office has built a foundation that can support a winning team soon. Baseball is a game of long seasons and hard lessons. This year, the lesson is that Miami has the right people to turn things around. From the dugout to the minor leagues, the signs of progress are clear for those willing to look. The team needs to be thankful for four specific areas that show real promise. Stability From the Ace Sandy Alcantara remains the anchor of the pitching staff when it matters most. He has shown no signs of quitting on a losing effort. Many stars would have demanded a trade or checked out mentally when the team struggled to win. Alcantara chose to stay and lead by example instead. His value goes beyond just throwing strikes on the mound. He acts as a high-road leader in the clubhouse, setting a tone for younger players to follow. This loyalty is rare in modern sports and gives the team a solid core to build upon. Young Stars Rise Up The infield and catching spots have found new life with two breakout performers. Javier Sanoja emerged as a key starter at third base by the second half of the season. He brings great contact skills and the ability to steal bases, making him a threat every time he steps to the plate. His defense is sharp, and he has become a go-to player for the lineup. Catcher Joe Mack arrived at age 23 and made an immediate impact behind the plate. Among the most gifted defensive catchers across the whole game, he surfaced. His performance suggests he will be electric in 2027. The Marlins were right to promote him, and he has become a blessing for the team. Flexibility and Future Arms Griffin Conine offers a different kind of value that often gets overlooked by fans. He is unselfish and willing to play any position the team needs, including first base. His professional attitude allows the manager to move him around without worrying about his reaction. According to Sports Illustrated , Conine said he is “striving to be more consistent.” The minor league system also shows signs of life with pitcher Jacob Kisting. His ability to command the ball and generate swings and misses makes him a top prospect for the future. Kisting could see the majors before the end of 2027 if he continues this path. These four players give the Marlins a clear path forward as the offseason begins. The team has the pitching, the defense, and the mindset needed to compete again soon.

After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
